column2: A planned frontier containing exactly one task returns run-leased-in-session with stable acquire, packet, and release commands; it never returns a worker group.
A single-repository plan with several ordinary tasks stays in the parent unless a genuinely parallel frontier contains multiple selected tasks.
Independent tasks in different repositories produce a bounded spawn-group and retain repository-specific packet authority.
The singleton inline path requires acquisition before packet generation, preserves fencing data, and releases only the matching owner.
An unexpired live lease returns wait and never duplicates inline or spawned execution after a host restart.
Expired lease takeover advances fencing generation and rejects a late result from the former owner.
A task cannot complete from a claimed result when observed writes exceed its allowed repository paths.
Dispatch and result acceptance reject stale graph revisions after tasks or dependencies change.
Build instructions completely and unambiguously explain run-in-session, run-leased-in-session, spawn-group, wait, blocked, and build-complete.
All runtime API 26 and protocol pins agree, and a mixed entrypoint/runtime installation fails before mutation.
A fresh temporary consumer install exposes runtime API 26, passes both doctors, and can invoke agent planning and dispatch commands.
Upgrading an older installed consumer neither leaves a torn runtime nor silently accepts incompatible state.
Public CLI commands and direct runtime commands map to the same lifecycle phase, including agent planning and dispatch operations.
Declared critical cases absent from the workspace block readiness, while tagged discoverable cases do not false-block.
Review responses preserve reviewer and subject provenance, cannot reuse authority, and cannot convert unknown blockers into zero.
Land refuses stale or missing proof, preserves root isolation before acceptance, and resumes safely after an interrupted archive.
Installed hooks block secret exfiltration without preventing safe documentation based on example variable names.
Unknown usage remains unknown rather than zero, blocked phases are not failures, and cache-write spend reaches budget accounting.
Dashboard evidence and blocker projections distinguish failed proof, awaiting proof, and genuinely blocked changes without treating proof.json as a provider.
The complete deterministic harness, wiring, and command registry remain coherent after the dispatch schema and runtime API bump.
